labels.label: T-abs-nested-causalities/1-gh
labels.notes: The iff is sharp. globallyHyperbolic_iff_of_nested (T2, x <=_M y => x <='_M y, C' GH) says C is GH iff every narrower diamond J_C(p,q) is closed. (=>) holds because compact sets are closed in a T2 space. (<=) holds because J_C(p,q) is a closed subset of the compact J_C'(p,q), and causality of C comes from C'. So the added hypothesis is necessary as well as sufficient, and nothing beyond it is assumed. It is close to a tautology, though: it is the compactness clause of GH, relativised to the wider diamonds. The mathematical content is the counterexample plus a one-line compactness argument. The counterexample is genuine. cutLine 0 is a Causality, LeNested in timelikeLine on every open set (cutLine_leNested), and causal. timelikeLine is GH (library). The cutLine diamond J(-1,1) = [-1,1] \ {0} is not closed. My probe also checked that cutLine a is <<-nested (LtNested), so the counterexample does not hinge on nesting <= only. The bare 'wider GH => narrower GH' is false (not_globallyHyperbolic_of_nested_bare). Mark: under the pseudo-label as dispatched ('with exactly the extra hypotheses needed') the iff plus the refutation answer the target in full, so the mark is defensible and Lean >= target. But the module's own checklist row (NestedCausalities.lean:61) classes the hypothesis as '⚠ strengthened', and kb/0011 says a strengthened row is not marked. That inconsistency is minor finding 2. The closedness hypothesis is not a ladder node (layer-1 rule). The sufficient variant of_nested_of_isClosed_J uses closed J^± of points, which is a ladder consequence of GH + tarentin + T2. The author should rule on keeping the mark (the closer's own question).

labels.label: T-abs-nested-causalities/2-dod
labels.notes: Marked partial and unmarked, correctly. D_C'(S) ⊆ D_C(S) and 'C'-Cauchy => C-Cauchy' hold under InextensibleNestedOn C C' W, which is a declared localisation (nesting) hypothesis. Both proofs are one line from it. The substantive part is the discharge on M, inextensibleNestedOn_top / GloballyHyperbolic.inextensibleNestedOn_top. It needs CurveNestedOn, causally arc-connected, causal, strongly causal, closed J^± and J^±(x) != {x}. The last is not a ladder node (disclosed; it is already a side condition of the ladder's Lemma K consequence). The witness timelikeLine_inextensibleNestedOn_top shows the discharge hypotheses are satisfiable. The counterexample is genuine. On cutLine 1, id over [1,+∞) is inextensible (nothing lies strictly below 1), {0} is timelikeLine-Cauchy and is missed, and 1 ∈ D_tl({0}) \ D_cut({0}). My probe proved explicitly that ¬ InextensibleNestedOn (cutLine 1) timelikeLine ⊤, via IsCauchySurfaceOn.of_nested. So LeNested does not imply InextensibleNestedOn. The REPORT calls InextensibleNestedOn 'the weakest form that works'; that is not proved (minor finding 5).

labels.label: T-abs-nested-causalities/3-ers-4.70
labels.notes: Partial and unmarked. ers_lemma_4_70 concludes that U1 ∩ U2 is preconnected (connected in the _isConnected form). It takes S preconnected, S Cᵢ-Cauchy in Uᵢ, Cτ causal, hthrough, honce (point-wise) and InextensibleNestedOn Cτ Cᵢ Uᵢ. Each hypothesis is separate and named. None contains the conclusion. The witness timelikeLine_ers_lemma_4_70 is degenerate (U1 = U2 = ℝ) but valid. The REPORT's finding about ERS's proof is wrong. Under ERS's own (4.62), integral curves of T are injective, so the two readings of 'at most once' coincide (major finding 1). For the same reason, hτ (Cτ causal) is a layer-3 consequence of (4.62), not a strengthening of ERS. The quote matches the LaTeX (erslem:LemConnected).

labels.label: T-abs-nested-causalities/3-ers-4.72

The finding that the first step of ERS's proof (lines 1811-1819, which uses u1 g(u1)-GH) is not needed with S acausal is true of the Lean proof (image_uIcc_subset_of_isCauchySurfaceOn). The witness timelikeLine_ers_lemma_4_72 is valid. The quote matches the LaTeX.

labels.label: T-abs-nested-causalities/3-ers-4.77
labels.notes: Partial and unmarked. The conclusion is 'S is a Cauchy surface of the union' (and that union is the greatest such open set), not 'Umax globally hyperbolic'. This is disclosed: Geroch (iii)=>(i) is the cited sorry of CausalScaffold.GerochEquiv, which I checked. hpair is S Cauchy in each pairwise intersection, supplied by Lemma 4.70 + Thm 4.64 / Remark 4.67, which says the intersection is the MCGHD under connectedness (checked in the LaTeX, ersrem:RemTime). hpair is about intersections, so it is not the conclusion (which is about the union) in disguise. hcaus (the union causal) is an addition ERS do not have. It is flagged openly as '⚠ strengthened' in the checklist (NestedCausalities.lean:70) and in the REPORT, not hidden. 'One causality on M agreeing with g(uα) on each Uα' is an interpretation carried by isCauchySurfaceOn_of_agree, with Cor 4.71 as supplier. The witness timelikeLine_ers_theorem_4_77 is valid (ι = Unit).

labels.label: T-abs-nested-causalities/3-ers-4.82
labels.notes: Partial and unmarked. hstep is not the conclusion in disguise. It is ERS's Steps 3-5 at a single boundary point: given p ∈ ∂A ∩ U₂ with (4.85) and a neighbourhood V ⊆ U₂ with V ∩ U₁ ⊆ A, some GHD strictly contains U₁. The Lean proves the rest: (4.84) for locally connected M, the (4.85) point by compactness and Zorn, p ∉ closure S, and the use of the one-sidedness. hstep still carries the larger part of ERS's proof, including 'u3 is a GHD'. This is disclosed. hstep is consistent with ERS: the chart of (4.83) is applied at a point q of Σ ∩ ∂A inside an arbitrarily small convex neighbourhood of p (Step 4 of Thm 4.64), so a layer-3 lemma assuming (4.83) can supply it. honesided is genuinely weaker than (4.83): shrink the base of the box by continuity of f so that every vertical fibre below the graph is a nonempty interval. The two readings of ∂S agree on ∂U₁ \ closure S, as the closer says. The finding 'no nesting in Thm 4.82; the cone condition enters only in Lemma 4.86 via (4.87)' is true to the LaTeX (ersthm:ThmNotBlocking, erslem:PropertyTimelike). ERS state (4.87) with Σ|δᵢ| < δ; the REPORT writes |δ| < δ₀, which is fine. The file has no witness for 4.82 (disclosed). My probe checked that a trivial instance satisfies every hypothesis (ι = Unit, dom = ⊤, cau = timelikeLine, S = {0}, s₀ = 0), so the hypotheses are jointly satisfiable.

findings.what: The finding says a gap in ERS Lemma 4.70's proof depends on the reading. It claims that, read set-wise, 'a periodic integral curve of T (possible for a non-vanishing field on R^{d+1}, d >= 2)' defeats the step at lines 1769-1771. That is false under ERS's hypotheses. In (4.61) g = g(u, du) has no x-dependence (LaTeX §4.1, theorems_intro; the same in §2, label general). So (4.62), 'T timelike w.r.t. g(u, du) for all u, du', makes T(x) timelike for the fixed constant Lorentz metric h = g(0,0) at every x (any value with g Lorentzian will do). T is continuous and never null on the connected R^{d+1}, so it stays in one time cone K of h. With e ∈ K, the linear map ℓ = -h(e, ·) is > 0 on K. Hence ℓ strictly increases along every integral curve of T. Integral curves are injective, T has no closed orbit, and the set-wise and parameter-wise readings of 'at most once' coincide. ERS's step follows under either reading. The REPORT would send the author a proof gap that does not exist.
findings.fix: Retract the finding. Replace it with: 'Under (4.62), T lies in one time cone of the constant metric g(0,0), so a linear function increases strictly along its integral curves. T has no closed orbit and both readings of at most once agree.' Reclassify the hypothesis row as 'named: a layer-3 consequence of (4.62)' instead of 'strengthened'. Answer the 4.70 question as moot. The Lean file needs no change; optionally add the reason to the checklist row at NestedCausalities.lean:63.
